title: Tim Berners-Lee's First Browser and the Birth of HTML (1990)
explainer: In November 1990, working alone on a NeXT computer at CERN, Tim Berners-Lee wrote both the first web browser/editor (which he called 'WorldWideWeb') and the first version of HTML, the markup language it was built to display. The tags you write today descend directly from a single researcher's attempt to let physicists share linked documents over a network - a much narrower original purpose than the web ended up serving.

title: Hakon Wium Lie and the Browser-Era Fight Over CSS (1994)
explainer: By 1994, competing browsers (Mosaic, early Netscape) were each inventing their own ad hoc presentation hacks, and HTML itself was under pressure to absorb layout tags it was never designed for. Hakon Wium Lie's October 1994 'Cascading HTML Style Sheets' proposal - refined with Bert Bos - introduced the specific idea of a 'cascade' that balances the document author's styling wishes against the reader's own preferences, which is why CSS rules can come from multiple sources and still combine predictably.
